retelling.text: Jesus glances up and sees wealthy people dropping their gifts into the temple treasury. Then He notices a poor widow who quietly places two tiny coins among them.
Jesus tells those around Him that this poor woman has given more than all the others. They gave out of their extra, but she, with so little, gave everything she had to live on.

reflectionTitle: Monday of the Thirty-fourth Week: Giving Our Whole Selves
reflection: As the Church year draws to a close, today's readings turn our eyes toward what truly lasts.
In the Book of Revelation, John sees the Lamb standing with a great company who belong to Him. They follow Him wherever He goes, and nothing false is found on their lips.
These are not people who gave God leftovers. They gave Him their whole lives.
The Psalm asks who may stand in the Lord's holy place, and answers: those with clean hands and a pure heart, who do not chase what is empty. It is the longing of a people who want to see God's face.
In the Gospel, Jesus watches the temple treasury, and what He notices is surprising. He does not admire the largest gifts. He sees one poor widow and her two small coins.
Her offering would never have been counted in any budget. Yet Jesus says it outweighs everything else, because the others gave from their surplus while she gave from her need.
That is challenging. Heaven measures generosity not by the size of the gift but by how much of ourselves is in it.
She also trusted. Giving away what she needed to live was an act of faith that God would provide.
The Alleluia tells us to stay awake. Part of staying awake is noticing people the way Jesus does, looking past status and titles to the quiet faithfulness others overlook.
In a workplace, that might mean recognizing the team member who never asks for credit but always carries more than their share. Those who lead are called to see them and thank them.
At home, it may be the time and patience we give when we are tired, not just when it is easy.
In our communities, it is giving to those in need without waiting until we feel we have plenty to spare.
Leadership in the spirit of Jesus means giving first and giving fully, and learning to value what is offered in love, however small it looks.
Today we can ask the Lord what He is inviting us to give wholeheartedly, whether that is our time, our attention or our trust.
message: God measures our gifts by the love and trust behind them, so give wholeheartedly, and look for the quiet faithfulness of others that deserves to be seen.
